# convoy_event_type (Resource)

An event type documents an event your project emits (e.g. `invoice.paid`) so customers can subscribe to it from the portal. Convoy cannot delete event types: destroying this resource **deprecates** the event type, and its name cannot be reused afterwards.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "convoy_event_type" "invoice_paid" {
  name        = "invoice.paid"
  category    = "billing"
  description = "Sent when an invoice is fully paid."
  json_schema = jsonencode({
    "$schema" = "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"
    type      = "object"
    required  = ["id", "amount"]
    properties = {
      id     = { type = "string" }
      amount = { type = "integer" }
    }
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Event type name, e.g. `invoice.paid`. Changing this forces a new event type (the old one is deprecated).

### Optional

- `category` (String) Product specific grouping, e.g. `billing`.
- `description` (String) What the event means.
- `json_schema` (String) JSON Schema of the event payload (use `jsonencode()` or `file()`).
- `project_id` (String) ID of the project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id`. Changing this forces a new object to be created.

### Read-Only

- `deprecated_at` (String) Deprecation timestamp, when deprecated outside Terraform.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier (`uid`) of the event type.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import convoy_event_type.invoice_paid 01H0JA5MEES38RRK3HTEJC647K/01H0JATTVCXZK8FRDX1M1JN3QY
```
